name: Albert Einstein
famous_quote: Imagination is more important than knowledge.
character_sheet: Albert as a 9-year-old boy with dark curly hair, warm brown eyes, a grey buttoned jacket over a white collared shirt and short trousers.
cover_scene: Albert as a 9-year-old boy with dark curly hair, warm brown eyes, a grey buttoned jacket over a white collared shirt and short trousers, sitting on a hillside holding a small brass compass as a beam of golden light stretches across the evening sky.
story_childhood:
In a town called Ulm,
by a wide German river,
a baby boy was born.

His name was Albert.

He did not talk much,
not for a long time.
His family began to wonder.

But inside his head,
quiet questions were growing.
Big, glowing, wonderful questions.
childhood_scene: A wide view of the old German town of Ulm, red rooftops and a tall cathedral spire beside the gentle Danube river, green hills rolling under a soft morning sky.
story_takeaway: Wonder about the world, and the world will whisper back its secrets.

chapters.title: The Magic Needle
chapters.narrative:
When Albert was small,
he felt quite sick in bed.

His father brought a gift.
A little pocket compass.

Albert turned it round and round.
The needle always pointed north.

Something invisible was pulling it!
He could not see it.
He could not touch it.

But it was real.
Albert never forgot that feeling.
chapters.scene: Albert as a 9-year-old boy with dark curly hair, warm brown eyes, a grey buttoned jacket over a white collared shirt and short trousers, lying propped in a wooden bed holding a small brass compass close to his wide, wondering eyes.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Asked Why
chapters.narrative:
School felt like marching.
Rules, rules, and more rules.

Albert liked to daydream instead.

He imagined riding a sunbeam.
How fast would the world rush by?

Teachers thought he was slow.
They were quite wrong.

He was thinking deep thoughts,
thoughts too big for the room.

At home he read and wondered,
and played his violin softly.
chapters.scene: Albert as a 9-year-old boy with dark curly hair, warm brown eyes, a grey buttoned jacket over a white collared shirt and short trousers, sitting by a window in a strict classroom, gazing out at sunbeams while other children copy from a chalkboard.

chapters.title: The Clerk with a Secret
chapters.narrative:
Albert grew into a young man.
No school wanted to hire him.

So he worked in an office,
stamping papers all day long.

But his mind kept flying.

At his little desk he dreamed
of light, and time, and space.

He scribbled ideas on scraps.
Could time run slow or fast?

One quiet clerk
was changing everything.
chapters.scene: A grown Albert with dark curly hair and warm brown eyes, wearing a modest early-1900s suit, sitting at a wooden patent-office desk crowded with papers, secretly sketching stars and clocks in a small notebook.

chapters.title: Riding the Beam of Light
chapters.narrative:
His ideas burst into the world.

He showed that time can bend.
That light and space are woven together.

People everywhere were amazed.

The shy, quiet boy
became the most famous mind on Earth.

Yet he stayed gentle and kind.

He still wondered like a child,
chasing sunbeams in his mind,
never, ever stopping.
chapters.scene: A grown Albert with wild silver hair and warm brown eyes stands on a vast dark hillside beneath a sky full of stars, arms open, as a single glowing beam of light curves and bends around him, lighting his awestruck face.

modern.title: If Albert Were 10 Today
modern.narrative:
Albert would love today's world.
He would watch space rockets roar
and ask a hundred questions.

He might build wobbly ramps,
test them again and again,
and giggle when things went wrong.

At night he would gaze at screens
showing galaxies far away.
Then he would grab his violin
and play a tune to the stars.
modern.scene: Albert as a 9-year-old boy with dark curly hair, warm brown eyes, a grey buttoned jacket over a white collared shirt and short trousers, lying on the floor of a modern bedroom watching a laptop screen full of galaxies, a toy rocket beside him.

timeline.caption: A pocket compass fills him with wonder.
timeline.scene: A small brass compass resting in an open child's palm, its needle glinting.

timeline.caption: A young clerk shares world-changing ideas.

timeline.caption: The dreamer's ideas light the whole world.
timeline.scene: A violin resting on a windowsill with starlight streaming through the glass.

after_treasures.title: Gifts That Live On
after_treasures.narrative:
Albert left us more than answers.

He left us questions,
bright as stars.

He showed that light can bend,
that time is not so simple.

He taught us to keep wondering,
to never stop asking why.

His gifts still glow today,
in every curious mind
that dares to dream.
after_treasures.scene: A softly glowing desk holding an open notebook, a compass, a violin, and a globe, with a window showing a star-filled sky.

treasures.name: A Lifetime of Curiosity
treasures.scene: An old worn notebook filled with sketches of stars, clocks, and question marks, lying open on a desk.

lessons.lesson: Dreaming big is where every discovery begins.
Keep asking why, even when others stop.
Great ideas grow slowly and quietly inside you.
The whole universe is waiting to amaze you.
